transitions-dev.note: Best value item in the batch. Buy the $149 lifetime, but confirm the commercial licence covers client deliverables first.

flaude.note: House rule: Flaude output gets fully restyled before it goes anywhere near a client deliverable.

refero-styles.note: Free browsing is a benchmarking reference. Get the Pro price in writing before wiring MCP into a workflow.

wonder-aquila-labs.note: Internal projects only while it is in public alpha — no Figma round-trip, so not for a client deadline.

appless-thesys.note: Read as a pattern study. The reusable asset is the schema-constrained render contract, not the phone-OS demo.

meat-bold-software.note: Try the Apache-2.0 tool before writing our own. Verify model cost on large diffs.

claude-model-and-effort-level-in-claude-.note: House default set from this: mid-tier model at medium for routine build work, top model at high only for architecture and debugging.

figma-make-kits.note: Publish one kit per retained client and treat it as a delivery artefact.

expo-expo.note: Follow @expo_status for incidents — @expo itself is the marketing feed.

designengineer-tools.note: Read once, diff against the studio stack, record adoptions in the Foundry wiki.

vercel-open-source-program.note: $3,600 of credit, but it creates a maintenance obligation. Only worth it if we open-source something real.

steering-claude-code-skills-hooks-rules-.note: Action: audit the .claude/ setup for Foundry and client repos against the seven mechanisms.

launch-kit.note: The default starting point for a new project — rules, commands, hooks and quality gates from day one.

flow.note: Our spec-to-shipped delivery loop. Use it on anything with more than a couple of days in it.

humanizer.note: Final pass on client-facing copy. It removes AI tells; it does not fix a weak argument.
